mainTopic: How to clean a non-Jew's winepress and its woven equipment: water and ashes, rinsing, waiting, hot water, and running water
overview: The גמרא explains how to clean a winepress that a non-Jew used. רב starts with water and then ashes, while רבה בר בר חנה starts with ashes and then water. They do not really argue: one speaks of a wet winepress and the other of a dry one. בי רב and שמואל then disagree about how many rounds of cleaning are needed, and the גמרא explains that in the Pumbedita version the gap is only about whether the final rinse counts. The students ask רבי אבהו how to clean gentiles' grape nets, and he answers from a ברייתא about impure presses. That ברייתא sorts the cleaning by material: rinsing, cleansing with ashes and water, or leaving the item unused for a year. רבי יוסי adds faster methods: boiling water, or leaving the item in running water for an עונה. The גמרא corrects the ברייתא's closing line so that יין נסך follows טהרות. It then defines an עונה as twelve hours, measured differently by season. Finally, רב יהודה explains how to clean gentiles' straining bags, baskets and strainers by their material, and his list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Water first or ashes first
steps.stepSummary: רב says to clean with water and then ashes. רבה בר בר חנה says to clean with ashes and then water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: with water, and the same with ashes. רבה בר בר חנה says: with ashes, and the same with water.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain how to clean the winepress, and they seem to give opposite orders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that you need water and ashes. The only question is which comes first. רב starts with water, and רבה בר בר חנה starts with ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashes, used as a scrubbing agent
And the same applies; here it means the second material is used afterward

phrases.english: Rav says: with water,
phrases.notes: He is talking about cleaning the non-Jew's winepress, which the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: and the same with ashes (afterward).

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: לְאֵפֶר,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana says: with ashes,
and the same with water (afterward).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: בְּמַיִם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: water then ashes. רבה בר בר חנה: ashes then water.

steps.title: Wet winepress versus dry winepress
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two do not argue. Ashes come first for a wet winepress, and water comes first for a dry one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree: this one is about a wet winepress, and that one is about a dry winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the apparent argument by showing that each opinion is about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wet winepress is already moist, so ashes go on first and are then rinsed with water. A dry winepress first needs water to wet it, and only then can the ashes work. So the order depends on the winepress's condition, not on a real argument.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree: this one is about a wet one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רבה בר בר חנה's ashes-first rule.

phrases.english: that one is about a dry one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי — הָא בְּרַטִּיבְתָּא, הָא בְּיַבִּשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the two opinions in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and רבה בר בר חנה argue about the order of cleaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are correct: ashes first for a wet winepress, water first for a dry one.
steps.whatToRemember: Wet winepress: ashes, then water. Dry winepress: water, then ashes.

steps.title: How many rounds: the Sura version
steps.stepSummary: בי רב in the name of רב say two rounds (wet) or three (dry). שמואל says three (wet) or four (dry).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: the school of רב say in רב's name: two or three. And שמואל says: three or four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument about how many rounds of water and ashes are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smaller number in each pair is for a wet winepress and the larger is for a dry one, which needs an extra opening round of water. שמואל requires one more round than בי רב in both cases.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר בֵּי רַב מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: It was stated: the school of Rav say in the name of Rav:
two or three (rounds),
phrases.notes: Two for a wet winepress (ashes, water), three for a dry one (water, ashes, water).

phrases.english: and Shmuel says: three or four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר בֵּי רַב מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמְרִי
steps.confusionAlert: Each pair of numbers is not one opinion choosing between two options. The first number is for a wet winepress and the second is for a dry one.

steps.title: How many rounds: the Pumbedita version
steps.stepSummary: In Pumbedita they taught the numbers higher: בי רב say three or four, and שמואל says four or five.
steps.simpleTranslation: In Sura they taught it this way. In Pumbedita they taught: the school of רב say in רב's name: three or four. And שמואל says: four or five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that the yeshiva in Pumbedita had a different version of the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Pumbedita version, each side's numbers are one higher than in the Sura version. שמואל is still one round above בי רב. This sets up the next step, which explains that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Sura, the yeshiva city founded by רב
Pumbedita, another major Babylonian yeshiva city

phrases.english: In Sura they taught it this way;
in Pumbedita they taught:
the school of Rav say in the name of Rav:
three or four,
and Shmuel says: four or five.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי, בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the argument in step 3

steps.title: Counting the final rinse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says בי רב and שמואל do not really argue. שמואל counts the last rinse with water, and רב does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree: one Sage counts the last water, and the other Sage does not count the last water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the one-round gap between רב and שמואל is only a matter of counting, not a real argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both require the same actual cleaning. At the end there is a rinse with water just to wash off the ashes. שמואל counts it as a round, so his numbers are higher. רב does not count it, since it is only there to remove the ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The last water, the final rinse

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
one Sage counts the last water,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל, which is why his numbers are one higher.

phrases.english: and the other Sage does not count the last water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי, מָר קָא חָשֵׁיב מַיָּא בָּתְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the gap in the Pumbedita version from step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל disagree about how much cleaning is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: They require the same cleaning. Only שמואל counts the final rinse of water as a round.
steps.whatToRemember: In the Pumbedita version, the argument between רב and שמואל is only about whether to count the final rinse that washes off the ashes.

steps.title: How do you clean the gentiles' grape nets?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי אבהו how to clean the woven nets that gentiles use to hold grapes while treading them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי אבהו: those woven nets of the gentiles, what is the way to clean them?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. The students ask רבי אבהו how to clean woven nets that soaked up gentile wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא discussed how to clean a winepress. A woven net is harder to clean because wine soaks into it. So the students want to know what process makes it usable.

keyTerms.meaning: Woven nets or baskets that hold the grapes during treading

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Abbahu:
Those wicker nets of the gentiles, what is their law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from cleaning the winepress itself to cleaning the woven nets used in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What cleaning process makes gentile grape nets usable?

steps.title: רבי אבהו answers from a ברייתא about impure presses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו cites a ברייתא. Hard parts are rinsed, palm and hemp baskets are cleansed with ashes and water, and bulrush and reed baskets must sit unused for twelve months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says to leave them from one pressing season to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: You already learned this in a ברייתא. If someone's winepresses and olive presses were impure and he wanted to press in purity, he rinses the planks, troughs and twigs. He wipes clean the baskets made of palm leaves or hemp. He leaves the baskets made of bulrush or reeds unused for twelve months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he leaves them from one wine season to the next, and from one olive season to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives cleaning rules for each part of a press.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about טומאה, not gentile wine, but the cleaning process is the same. How much a material absorbs decides how it is cleaned. Hard parts only need rinsing, palm and hemp need cleansing with ashes and water, and bulrush and reeds soak up so much that only waiting a long time works.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a ברייתא)
He leaves them unused, lets them get old
From one wine-pressing season to the next

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא talks about טומאה (impure presses), not gentile wine. רבי אבהו uses it because the way to clean out what was absorbed is the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said to them: You learned it:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ גִּתָּיו וּבֵית בַּדָּיו טְמֵאִין,
phrases.english: One whose winepresses and olive presses were impure,
and he wanted to make them (his wine and oil) in purity —
the planks, the troughs, and the twig brooms, he rinses them;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָעֲקָלִין שֶׁל נְצָרִין וְשֶׁל בִּצְבּוּץ מְנַגְּבָן,
phrases.english: and the pressing baskets of palm leaves and of hemp, he cleanses them (with ashes and water);
and those of bulrush and of reeds,
he leaves them unused for twelve months.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He leaves them from wine-pressing to wine-pressing, and from olive-pressing to olive-pressing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: תְּנֵיתוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Woven items are treated by material: palm and hemp are cleansed with ashes and water, while bulrush and reeds are left unused for twelve months (or a full season, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל).

steps.title: Isn't רבן שמעון בן גמליאל the same as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference there is between twelve months and one season to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a question about the ברייתא. One pressing season to the next is about twelve months, so the two opinions seem to say the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two תנאים say the same thing, there is no point in recording a separate opinion. So the גמרא wants to find the practical difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: That is the same as the first tanna!
phrases.notes: From one season to the next is roughly a year, just like the twelve months of the first opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Season to season equals twelve months, so his opinion adds nothing new.

steps.title: The difference is early and late harvests
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions differ when the harvest comes earlier or later than a full year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is early and late harvests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two opinions differ when the time between seasons is not exactly twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא needs a full twelve months. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only needs the next season, which could come a little before or after twelve months. If next year's grapes ripen early, he lets you use the baskets sooner.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: early-ripening and late-ripening crops.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference between the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Season to season is just another way of saying twelve months.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes by the actual next harvest, even if it comes before or after a full twelve months.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's quick way: boiling water or olive water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that someone who wants to purify the baskets right away can pour boiling water over them or scald them in olive water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Someone who wants to purify them right away pours boiling water over them, or scalds them in olive water.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי. He gives a fast way to clean the baskets so you don't have to wait a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waiting lets the absorbed liquid dry out slowly. Hot water pushes it out right away, the same idea as הגעלה for utensils.

keyTerms.meaning: He purges them with boiling water (הגעלה)
Water that olives were cooked in

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הָרוֹצֶה לְטַהֲרָן מִיָּד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: One who wants to purify them right away
purges them with boiling water,
or scalds them in olive water.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הָרוֹצֶה לְטַהֲרָן מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 7 and adds another opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baskets can be purified right away with boiling water or hot olive water.

steps.title: Running water for an עונה
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל quotes רבי יוסי: put the baskets under a flowing pipe or in a fast spring, for an עונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי יוסי: He puts them under a pipe whose water keeps flowing, or in a spring whose water runs fast. And for how long? An עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more quick method, washing out the baskets in running water. It ends with how long to leave them there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a cold-water method, but the water has to keep flowing so it carries the absorbed liquid away. The ברייתא says to leave them an עונה but does not say how long that is. The גמרא will explain it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A set period of time (defined later)

steps.whatToRemember: A press's woven baskets can be made usable in three ways: wait a year (or a season), use hot water right away, or leave them in running water for an עונה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
He places them under a pipe whose water keeps flowing,
or in a spring whose water runs fast.
And for how long? An interval.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רבי יוסי's quick method, this time with running water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving the baskets in strongly running water for an עונה purifies them.

steps.title: The ברייתא compares wine rules to purity rules
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes by saying that the cleaning rules taught for יין נסך were taught the same way for טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same way the Sages said these cleaning rules about libation wine, they said them about purity matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one last line. As worded, it makes יין נסך the base and says the same cleaning methods were taught for טהרות. This line sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא listed ways to clean impure winepress equipment: rinsing, cleansing with ashes and water, waiting, scalding, and flowing water. So its topic has been טהרות all along. Yet this line is worded as if יין נסך is the source and טהרות copies it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same way that they said
Wine poured as an offering to עבודה זרה, which is forbidden

phrases.english: In the same way that they said regarding libation wine,
so they said regarding purity matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיֵין נֶסֶךְ, כָּךְ אָמְרוּ בִּטְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the closing line of the same ברייתא quoted in steps 7, 10 and 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cleaning methods for יין נסך apply the same way to טהרות.

steps.title: The comparison is backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא's comparison runs in the wrong direction, because the topic here is טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the opposite! We are dealing with purity matters!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the line in step 12. It says the comparison was made in the wrong direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you say "just as in A, so too in B," A is the base and B copies it. The גמרא says טהרות is the topic we are dealing with here, so טהרות should be the base, not יין נסך. The line in step 12 has the order reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the opposite! (an expression saying something is backwards)
We are dealing with, we are standing in

phrases.english: It is the opposite!
phrases.notes: Literally, "toward the other side!" It is a way of saying "you have it backwards."

phrases.english: We are dealing with purity matters!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלַפֵּי לְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the wording of the comparison in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The direction of the comparison in step 12, which makes יין נסך the base.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The topic being dealt with is טהרות, so טהרות should be the base and יין נסך should be compared to it, not the other way around.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: wine follows purity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא so that it says יין נסך follows the rules of טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: the same way they said these rules about purity matters, they said them about libation wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from step 13 by flipping the line around. Now טהרות is the base and יין נסך copies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not rejected. Only its wording is corrected. The cleaning rules still apply to both areas, but the source is now טהרות and יין נסך learns from it.
steps.confusionAlert: Both versions say the same cleaning rules apply to both areas. The only change is which area is the base and which one copies it.

phrases.english: Rather: in the same way that they said regarding purity matters,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the wording, so read the ברייתא this new way.

phrases.english: so they said regarding libation wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּטְהָרוֹת, כָּךְ אָמְרוּ בְּיֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the objection in step 13 by reversing the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא sounded as if יין נסך was the base and טהרות copied it.
steps.terutzMaskana: טהרות is the base, and the same rules carry over to יין נסך.
steps.whyThisMatters: It tells us that the cleaning methods for a winepress used by a non-Jew are modeled on the laws of טהרות.

steps.title: How long is an עונה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long the עונה is that רבי יוסי required in step 11.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long is an עונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to step 11, where the baskets had to sit under flowing water for one עונה. It asks how long that is. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 gave a length of time without explaining it. To follow the rule in practice, you need to know how long an עונה is. This is a simple question to define a term, not a challenge.

phrases.english: How long is an interval?

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה עוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the comparison, the גמרא returns to define the term used in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of an עונה.

steps.title: First answer: a full day or a full night
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that רבי יוחנן said an עונה is either a whole day or a whole night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: an עונה is either a day or a night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to the question in step 15. According to this report, an עונה is one full day or one full night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer measures an עונה as one complete stretch of daylight or one complete stretch of darkness. You do not need both together. One whole period of either one is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Either a day or a night

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Either a day or a night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עונה is one full day or one full night.

steps.title: Second answer: half a day and half a night
steps.stepSummary: A different chain of rabbis reports that רבי יוחנן said an עונה is half a day plus half a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנא שאינה (some say רבי חנא בר שאינה) said in the name of רבה בר בר חנה, in the name of רבי יוחנן: an עונה is half a day and half a night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רבי יוחנן said. This report gives a different length: half a day joined with half a night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports quote רבי יוחנן, but they seem to disagree. In this version the עונה is made up of part of a day and part of a night joined together, not one whole day or one whole night. This sets up a contradiction that the next step will resolve.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a day and half a night

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥana Sha'ina,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי חָנָא בַּר שְׁאִינָה,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Ḥana bar Sha'ina,
said that Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Half a day and half a night.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָנָא שְׁאִינָה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי חָנָא בַּר שְׁאִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives a competing report of רבי יוחנן's answer that seems to contradict step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עונה is half a day and half a night.

steps.title: No real argument: it depends on the season
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר יצחק explains that the two reports do not argue. Each one describes a different season.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר יצחק said: they do not disagree. One answer is for the seasons of ניסן and תשרי, and the other is for the seasons of תמוז and טבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the apparent contradiction between steps 16 and 17. Both answers are correct, each for a different time of year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Around ניסן and תשרי, day and night are equal, so a whole day or a whole night is exactly twelve hours. Around תמוז and טבת, one is long and the other is short, so you take half a day plus half a night to reach the same twelve hours. Both reports describe the same length of time measured in different seasons.

keyTerms.meaning: Season of the year (the time around an equinox or solstice)
This one... that one (splitting two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: An עונה is twelve hours. When day and night are equal (ניסן and תשרי), that is a full day or a full night. When they are unequal (תמוז and טבת), it is half a day plus half a night.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:
And they do not disagree;
this one is in the season of Nisan and Tishrei,
phrases.notes: This is the "day or night" answer from step 16. In these seasons day and night are equal.

phrases.english: that one is in the season of Tammuz and Tevet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי, הָא בִּתְקוּפַת נִיסָן וְתִשְׁרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This resolves the apparent contradiction between steps 16 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by case: each statement applies to a different season
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports of רבי יוחנן seemed to give two different lengths for an עונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both give the same twelve hours: a full day or night when they are equal, and half of each when they are unequal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical, fixed measure for how long the baskets must stay under flowing water at any time of year.

steps.title: Cleaning non-Jews' straining bags by material
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a non-Jew's straining bag made of hair is rinsed, one of wool is scrubbed, and one of flax is left unused for a while. Any knots must be untied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Non-Jews' straining bags made of hair are rinsed. Those made of wool are scrubbed clean. Those made of flax are left unused for a time. And if there are knots, he must untie them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב יהודה about how to make non-Jews' wine-straining bags usable again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method gets stricter as the material gets more able to soak up wine. Hair gets a simple rinse (הדחה), wool needs scrubbing, and flax needs the strongest treatment of all, being left unused (יישון). Knots must be untied because wine can stay trapped inside them.

keyTerms.meaning: Straining bags used to strain wine from its sediment
Scrubs them clean (with ashes and water)
Leaves them unused for a period of time (יִשּׁוּן)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Those straining bags of non-Jews
those of hair — one rinses them,
those of wool — one scrubs them clean,
phrases.notes: Literally "dries them," but here it means a real scrubbing, stronger than a rinse.

phrases.english: those of flax — one leaves them unused for a time,
and if there are knots — he unties them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הָנֵי רְוָוקֵי דַּאֲרַמָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of how long an עונה is. It moves to practical rules for cleaning specific utensils used with non-Jews' wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straining bags: hair is rinsed, wool is scrubbed, flax is left unused for a time. Knots must be untied.

steps.title: Cleaning non-Jews' baskets and strainers woven from palm strips
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה continues: baskets and strainers woven with palm-strip cords are rinsed. The list goes on at the start of the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those baskets and strainers of non-Jews that are woven with cords of palm strips are rinsed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה starts a second list, about baskets and strainers. He gives the first case here, and the list continues afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the straining bags, the material decides the cleaning. Baskets and strainers woven from palm strips need only a simple rinse. Other materials, which come next, may need more.

phrases.english: Those baskets and strainers of non-Jews
that are woven with cords of palm strips — one rinses them,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי דִּקוּלֵי וְחַלָּאתָא דַּאֲרַמָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's teaching, moving from straining bags to baskets and strainers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Baskets and strainers woven from palm strips need only rinsing.
